title: Introduce fallback choreography simulator and slim schema verifier for routing policies
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: The current policy validator surface focuses primarily on static schema checks and simple lint rules. It misses class of runtime failures where tier/region routing + model-variant fallbacks interact under capacity constraints (e.g., fallback thrashing, cross-region cascade, and cold-start latency amplification).

Goal: Implement a two-part surface: 1) a lightweight, deterministic schema verifier that is fast enough to run in CI and in the policy editor (Console) and provides actionable autofix suggestions; 2) a sandboxed fallback choreography simulator that can execute routing rules against stochastic workload traces to surface dangerous fallback sequences and quantify expected misroutes and latency regressions.

Scope:
- Design and implement a compact schema verifier ("slim verifier") that validates structure, type, constraint invariants, and compatibility across model variant families. Integrate with Console editor for near-instant feedback.
- Build a sandbox runtime that executes routing policies deterministically against replayed request traces and synthetic failure injections (region outage, capacity drain, model-unavailable). Produce scorecard metrics (misroute-rate, fallback-depth, median fallback latency, hot-queue probability).
- Add CI gate that runs the slim verifier; add optional pipeline step to run simulator for high-risk policy changes (label opt-in).
- Provide developer tooling: `policy-sim` CLI, JSON trace format, and a Compact HTML report for Designers/PMs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Slim verifier implements all required schema rules listed in the design doc and surfaces human-readable autofix suggestions for >= 80% of common errors.
- Simulator reproduces three canonical failure scenarios from incident playbook and reports metrics within expected tolerances.
- Console shows verifier errors inline within 300ms for policies up to 2.5KB.
- CI checks block merges on critical verification failures; optional simulator runs produce artifacts linked in PRs.

Design trade-offs:
- We prioritize speed and clear UX for the slim verifier over exhaustive semantic analysis; heavier semantic checks will live in separate offline validators.
- The simulator will run in deterministic mode for CI and stochastic mode for `policy-sim` runs; full-scale probabilistic fuzzing is out of scope for this ticket.

Implementation plan:
1) Schema: codify rules in a concise JSON-schema plus additional predicate checks implemented in Rust (shared with runtime) and a thin TypeScript wrapper for Console/CI.
2) Simulator: implement a sandboxed interpreter that mirrors the production policy decision graph but restricts side effects and replaces external calls with mocked telemetry/capacity profiles.
3) CI/Console integration: add verifier step to `policy-lint` action and embed TypeScript verifier in Console editor.
4) Docs & Onboarding: Confluence design doc, `policy-sim` README, and demo notebooks.

Metrics to monitor:
- PR block rate from verifier (false positives/negatives), target < 2% FP.
- Simulator-detected critical fallback sequences per month.
- Post-rollout production misroute rate compared to baseline (target reduction 30%).

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: merge slim verifier + Console integration behind feature flag; run on internal policies.
- Week 2: enable CI gate on engineering repos for policy changes.
- Week 3: pilot simulator runs on staging traffic + runbook review.
- Week 4: opt-in release to all customers for policy dry-run reports, iterate on autofix UX.

Notes & references:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Policy+Fallback+Choreography+Design
- Simulator prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/policy-sim/pull/78
- Incident playbook cases: #INC-2025-03-outage-routing and postmortem: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/fallback-playbook.pdf
